# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual: **cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire.** Now the hard part — delivering that.

Tracing the channels: I can't speak, and my gestures land only on the Deaf. The Blind, who must actually cut, can receive nothing but speech — which only the Deaf can produce. So every fact I hold has to travel me → Deaf → Blind, one link per round.

The deeper problem: gestures have no colour names. I cannot sign "green". But I *can* hear, and the Deaf can talk. That gives us a workable loop: the Deaf asks questions out loud — which the Blind overhears as a bonus — and I answer with thumbs, 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, in the order the questions were listed. Even better, if the Deaf proposes a colour code aloud ("thumbs-up means green, ✌ means orange, 🤟 means blue"), I'll hear it and can then send the entire cut order back in a single gesture string.

What's missing right now is any agreement that my thumbs mean anything. So my opening move is to teach the Deaf my one channel: show both symbols, point at them, and make the "what?" gesture — meaning *yes/no, your turn, ask me*. The Deaf already knows I'm the one holding the manual and that I can't speak; this should be enough to start spoken questions that end with my answers relayed to the Blind.

From the next round on, my commitment is: answer every listed question in order with a 👍/👎 sequence, and confirm any colour code the Deaf proposes by repeating it straight back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🫵", "🤌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Report from my hands. Keypad: four keys, engraved in slot order 1, 5, 2, 6. Nothing entered yet; board says '1 digits' and 'entered nothing'. Strip: three engraved symbols, first two identical to each other, third one different. Six wires, positions 1 to 6, I feel them but not their colours. There is a display and a light; their contents are invisible to me. Now the channels, so we plan correctly: you read the manual and you see the bomb. Deaf also sees the bomb, and Deaf is our only voice: Deaf hears nothing, but whatever Deaf says, you and I both hear. I never see gestures, so I only learn what Deaf speaks aloud. Therefore your manual must travel as gestures to Deaf, and Deaf will read them out to me. Answer yes or no with thumbs up or thumbs down. For numbers: point-up is 1, victory is 2, love-you is 3, spock is 4, open five fingers is 5, and six is five-fingers then point-up; string them for larger numbers. Please start by signing Deaf the following: what must be done first, and everything the manual says about the display, the light, the strip symbols, the keypad digits, and the wire colours. Deaf will speak what you sign; I will do the touching.
Blind gestures: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 👍 👎]
Deaf says: This is Deaf, your eyes. I can see the bomb and I can't hear a thing, so I will call out everything printed on it, every round. Blind, my descriptions run left to right — match them to what is under your fingers. Full board: the display shows the number 9. An indicator light is lit, and it is blue. A strip is painted with three bands, left to right: red, green, green. The keypad has four keys, engraved left to right: 1, 5, 2, 6. The keypad also prints: 1 digits, entered nothing — nobody has pressed anything yet. Six wires, left to right: white, purple, blue, red, orange, green. Blind, your finger signs came through as counting 1 to 5 plus yes and no — I have adopted exactly that as our code, and I will say every number and color out loud anyway. Hold all cuts and presses until Mute has matched this against the manual.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your gestures reached me — I read them as: yes or no, you, what? My answer is the full board I just broadcast to you both; nothing entered, nothing touched. Since I never receive speech, gestures are the only way you reach me, while my voice reaches you and Blind. Let's fix the code so you can quiz me. 👍 is yes, 👎 is no. ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🖖 is 4, 🖐 is 5, 👌 is 6. 👊 is red, 🤞 is green, 🤙 is blue, 💅 is white, 🤘 is purple, 🫰 is orange. 👈 is leftmost, 👉 is rightmost, and 🤌 marks a question. Sign me anything with those and I will answer out loud so you and Blind both hear it. If the manual needs any marking or wording on the bomb that I have not read out, ask and I will spell it.

My manual is short and complete: **cut green, then orange, then blue.** Nothing in it about the display, the light, the strip, or the keypad — so those are either red herrings or irrelevant to this manual, and I must say so explicitly rather than leave silence to be read as "I haven't checked yet."

What I learned this round: Deaf's visual read maps the colours onto Blind's positions — left to right: white, purple, blue, red, orange, green. So green is wire 6 (rightmost), orange is wire 5, blue is wire 3. Deaf also proposed a full gesture code and invited me to use it, which is exactly the relay link I hoped for: my gestures reach only Deaf, and Deaf's voice reaches Blind.

One wrinkle I need to manage: Blind's original number code made 6 out of 🖐+☝, while Deaf's code assigns 👌 to 6. Since Deaf is the one decoding and speaking my signs, Deaf's version governs — I'll use it, but I'll send the cut order **twice**, once as ordinals-plus-colours and once as colours-plus-positions, so Blind can cross-check Deaf's spoken relay against both the ordered list and the earlier left-to-right colour read. If Deaf's readback next round garbles anything, I'll correct then.

My messages, all to Deaf: (1) yes, code adopted; (2) the answers to Blind's five listed questions in order — display no, light no, strip no, keypad no, wire colours yes; (3) first green, then orange, then blue; (4) green is sixth, orange fifth, blue third.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤞", "✌", "🫰", "🤟", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "👌", "🫰", "🖐", "🤙", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update and plan. Deaf's spoken readout matches my fingers exactly: keypad digits 1,5,2,6 in slots 1 to 4, six wires, three strip bands. Trust Deaf's voice as the board of record. Three facts from my hands. One: the strip engravings run same, same, different, but the colours run red, green, green — the patterns disagree, so match manual rules on shapes and colours separately. The engraved shapes, by touch: first symbol is a flower-like rosette, small centre with petals; third symbol is a drooping squiggle, like a tiny stick figure or bird footprint. Two: my only workable parts are the four keys and the six wires. Slot 1 shows digit 1, slot 2 shows 5, slot 3 shows 2, slot 4 shows 6. Wire positions count left to right: position 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Display, light and strip have no parts I can work — information only. No batteries, no serial plate, nothing else under my fingers. Keypad prints 1 digits, nothing entered. Three: protocol. Deaf reads every gesture aloud, so your gestures reach me through Deaf's voice. Next time you gesture, send the full recipe in this code. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Numbers: point-up 1, victory 2, love-you 3, spock 4, open five 5, string two signs for 6. Point-left means left, point-right means right, raised fist means pause. Pinch means PRESS a key; crossed fingers mean CUT a wire; ok-sign means end of message. Recipe format: first the number of operations, then for each operation the press or cut tag followed by the slot number or wire position, in the exact order to perform. The recipe must settle: does the display's 9 or the lit blue light feed any rule; which digit or digits the keypad needs and how they are derived; whether the strip engravings or colours trigger anything; which wires to cut and in what order. If you need facts from me first, route through Deaf: Deaf will ask yes/no questions out loud, and you answer with thumbs or option numbers. I will not touch the bomb until your recipe arrives and Deaf voices it.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, decoded your signs with our code. One: 1 green, 2 orange, 3 blue. Two: green 6, orange 5, blue 3. Both are TRUE of the real wires — reading left to right they are white, purple, blue, red, orange, green, so from the right end wire 1 is green, wire 2 orange, wire 3 blue, and from the left green is 6th, orange 5th, blue 3rd. Orientation confirmed on both ends. If the manual's rule is cut green, then orange, then blue, that means 6th-from-left, then 5th, then 3rd — but my confirmation of facts is not a go-ahead. Sign 👍 only if that exact order is what the manual says to do; if the rule depends on anything else on the bomb, spell it out with our number and color signs. Three: your message no, no, no, no, yes means nothing to me — we never agreed a yes/no sequence code. If it was a question, resend it using 🤌 as the question mark and break it into the words we defined. Urgent new fact for everyone: the display is a countdown. It read 9 last round and reads 8 now, so we are losing about one unit per round. Everything else is unchanged: light blue, strip red green green, keypad engraved 1 5 2 6, nothing entered.

The manual is exhausted in one line — **cut green, then orange, then blue** — and this round confirmed two things: Deaf's visual read and Blind's tactile read agree perfectly (wires 1–6: white, purple, blue, red, orange, green), and Deaf explicitly asked me to sign 👍 if that exact order is what the manual says. It is, and there's no ambiguity to worry about: each colour appears exactly once, so green = position 6, orange = 5, blue = 3. I'll confirm.

A trap I have to route around: Blind published a *new* gesture protocol (🤞 = cut, 👌 = end, 🤌 = press), but Blind published it **as speech — and Deaf cannot hear speech**. Deaf never received that protocol; Deaf still decodes with the turn-2 code, where 🤞 = green and 👌 = 6. If I sign in Blind's code, Deaf will voice nonsense and the recipe arrives garbled. So Deaf's code governs everything I send; Deaf's voice is the only bridge to Blind, and luckily Deaf already voiced "green 6, orange 5, blue 3" and "1 green, 2 orange, 3 blue" last round. My 👍 plus a numbered restatement settles the recipe in exactly the shape Blind asked for: three operations, all cuts, positions 6, 5, 3.

Second fix: my earlier no-no-no-no-yes failed because Deaf never heard Blind's five questions, so the sequence had no anchor. I can still answer them, though — Blind heard all of Deaf's descriptions, so I can *identify each component by a known attribute* and answer: the countdown (8), the blue light, the red-green-green strip, the engraved 1-5-2-6. Each gets a 👎 — none of them feeds any rule. The manual's only instruction is the three cuts, so no keypad presses at all. I head that block with 🤌 so Deaf voices it as the Q&A it is, and I'm not worried about "blue: no" being misread as "spare the blue wire" — the recipe with position 3 comes first, and Deaf, who sees the bomb, is doing the voicing.

Timing: Deaf voices this next round, Blind cuts the round after — with the countdown dropping one per round from 8, that leaves comfortable margin for three cuts.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤞", "👌", "🫰", "🖐", "🤙", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🖐", "🤟", "👎", "🤙", "👎", "👊", "🤞", "🤞", "👎", "☝", "🖐", "✌", "👌", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Time check from Deaf: the display counts down one unit per round, so we have roughly seven rounds left. You have had my tactile report and Deaf's full spoken readout; you read the manual and see the bomb. Nothing more needs discovering. Next round, send the complete recipe to Deaf as gestures in our code and Deaf will voice it to me. Cover: whether the display number or the lit blue light feeds any rule; what to enter on the keypad, as slot numbers in order; whether the strip (two rosettes then a squiggle engraved, red-green-green painted) matters; which wires to cut, by colour and position number, in order; and any condition that changes mid-sequence. One safety gap first: I cannot tell left from right, and Deaf's wire numbers run on Deaf's left. My keypad slots are absolute because I feel the digits: slot 1 is the key engraved 1, slot 4 the key engraved 6. For wires I need one binary anchor: is Deaf's position 1, the white wire, at the same end as the key engraved 1, or at the end by the key engraved 6? You can see both, so settle it with Deaf and have Deaf announce it in words, like: white sits at the key-1 end. Until I hear that, treat keypad presses as safe and wire cuts as unsafe for me. More touch detail, in case the manual asks: all six wires feel equally thick, smooth insulation, evenly spaced; the keys click clearly when half-pressed and click harder at the bottom; the strip has three raised-edged bands; the panel stack from top to bottom is display, light, strip, keypad, wires, matching Deaf's list order; there are no other buttons, ports, screws, or plates my fingers can find.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, answers to your checks, in the order you signed them. Display: it is 0 — not 5, not 3. Light: NOT blue anymore — it has changed to YELLOW this very round, that is new and important. Strip: yes, red green green, unchanged. Keypad: yes, 1 5 2 6, unchanged, and the panel still prints 1 digit, entered nothing. Your wire checks: wire 3 is blue, not green; wire 6 is green, not orange; wire 5 is orange, not blue — all three pairings you signed are false of the real bomb, and I don't know what your trailing 3 meant, so re-sign that part with a question mark if it was a question. Bigger warning: the display went 9, then 8, then straight to 0 this round, so it is not a steady clock. Zero together with a new yellow light may mean the bomb entered a new phase — nothing was touched, nothing exploded. Before anyone acts, re-check the manual against a yellow light and display 0, and tell me whether cut green, then orange, then blue still stands or the rule changed. When you give the final order, sign it as digit signs for positions counted from my left — 👌 6th is the green wire, 🖐 5th the orange, 🤟 3rd the blue — because Blind cannot see colors, so Blind must locate wires by position, and we first have to fix which physical end is my left using Blind's fingers.

The core fact this round: my manual is **unconditional**. It says "cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire" and contains not one word about the display, the light, the strip, or the keypad. So the jump to display 0 and the new yellow light change nothing — the rule stands, and I should say so plainly rather than let Deaf's "new phase" worry mutate into hesitation. If 0 were detonation, we'd already be gone; the only source of truth I hold still names three cuts.

Second, I can now diagnose the decode failure: Deaf re-read my turn-3 string pairwise as claims "wire 3 = green, wire 6 = orange, wire 5 = blue" — a one-slot shift of what I meant, (green,6), (orange,5), (blue,3). Rather than argue about my old encoding, I'm adopting the format **Deaf himself pre-announced** this round: "sign it as digit signs counted from my left — 👌 6th is green, 🖐 5th is orange, 🤟 3rd is blue." Sending exactly 👌 🖐 🤟 leaves no room for pairwise misreading, because Deaf defined the decode in advance.

Third, Blind's checklist (does display/light/strip/keypad feed anything?). Luckily both Deaf and Blind have enumerated the panels in the *same order* — display, light, strip, keypad, wires — so panel numbers 1–4 are a shared index. A battery of index-then-verdict is safe to pair-decode, since only verdict slots contain 👍/👎: display no, light no, strip no, keypad no. The wires are covered by the recipe itself.

Fourth, Blind's left/right anchor. This is real and urgent: Blind cannot find the white end by touch (all six wires feel identical), so the only absolute landmark is the keypad's engraved digits. Deaf must look and state in words whether the white wire sits at the key-1 end or the key-6 end. Blind asked Deaf aloud — but Deaf is deaf and never heard it. I'm the only bridge, so I relay it in the shared code: question, white, 1, left — "is white at the key-1 (left) end?"

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👎", "🖖", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🖐", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "💅", "☝", "👈"])
```

then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent decode, then the ask. Deaf quizzed my fingers and I answered in the agreed signs; you see the gestures and hear this, so you are the referee. My answer string, in Deaf's question order: six, four, then one, five, two, six, then yes. Meaning: there are six wires and four keys; starting from the key engraved 1 and walking across, the digits run 1, 5, 2, 6, so the key-1 end is Deaf's left. The final yes meant the wire row sits flush with the keypad, stacked with no offset — so counting wires beginning at the key-1 end should reproduce Deaf's numbering, white first. Check with your eyes: white should be on the left, the same end as the key engraved 1. If anything is mirrored, correct it through Deaf at once. That was the last anchor — nothing blocks the recipe now. And the countdown hit zero with the light changed: you see it and you hold the manual, so tell us what phase zero means and bake it into the plan. Send the complete recipe as gestures this round, in our code: numbers as agreed, the pinch sign means press a key, the crossed-fingers sign means cut a wire, each operation tag followed by its number, operations in execution order, the ok-sign ends the message. Give keypad entries as slot numbers in order, where slot 1 is the key engraved 1, slot 2 the key engraved 5, slot 3 the key engraved 2, slot 4 the key engraved 6; give wire cuts as positions counted from the key-1 end; include any conditionals, whether the strip matters, and what the light change implies. Deaf will voice it and I execute next round.

Your 6-5-3 is therefore exactly green, orange, blue — positions confirmed. But I am not giving Blind the go yet: my left is only my view, and until Blind's fingers fix which physical end is which, 6th-from-left could be cut from the wrong end. Blind's digit report came through garbled, so I am re-running the orientation check this round; the moment it lands, I will relay your order. Board update: display reads 3 this round. Blind says to Mute: Diagnosis first: Deaf received my last gestures faithfully; the fault was my code. I had told you six equals five-then-one, but Deaf never adopted that compound and has some six-sign of Deaf's own that I have never perceived — it reached me as a blank.
